newsitem.title: CHINA: China says good care being taken of ex-official.
newsitem.headline: China says good care being taken of ex-official.

text.p: A former senior Chinese official who disappeared into effective house arrest after his release from prison last May is waiting for new housing and is well cared for, a top justice official said on Monday.

After a briefing to defend China's human rights record, executive vice-minister of justice Zhang Xiufu also said jailed former student leader Wang Dan was in good health and did not meet the criteria for medical parole.

Former official Bao Tong has been held at a state dormitory near Beijing since he was freed after serving seven years in jail for his role in 1989 pro-democracy protests, but Zhang said the former top aide was waiting to be assigned a new home.
"High-level departments think he is not suitable any more for ministerial-level housing and want to change his residence but have so far failed to do so," he said when asked about Bao's whereabouts.

Bao held ministerial status when he was secretary to the Communist Party's powerful Politburo in the late 1980s. He was the most senior official to be jailed after the 1989 pro-democracy demonstrations.
"Because a two-year suspension of his political rights still applies to Bao Tong, so some administrative bodies are exercising management measures," Zhang told a news conference.
Bao's case has drawn fire from the United States, which has protested against his detention without recourse to judicial representation and without access to his family.
Zhang defended Bao's detention, saying Beijing's measures were necessary and required by law. "The relevant departments are taking good care of him," he said.

Bao, once an aide to former Communist Party chief Zhao Ziyang who was sacked after the 1989 student-led demonstrations, was convicted of "counter-revolutionary incitement" and the leaking of state secrets.

Diplomats in Beijing say Bao is a source of anxiety for China's leaders, who fear he may reveal details of the dealings of the highest party echelons in the weeks before the bloody 1989 crackdown on demonstrators.
In remarks to reporters after the briefing, Zhang said jailed dissident Wang Dan was in good health and had recently taken part in a singing contest at his jail in northeastern China.

Wang's family and human rights groups have repeatedly raised concerns about the failing health of Wang, a leader of the 1989 pro-democracy protests in Beijing who was last year sentenced to 11 years in jail for plotting to overthrow the government.
Wang's condition did not merit medical parole, Zhang said but gave no details.
